overview: The 16x2 LCD (16 characters per line, 2 lines — a 20x4 version with more room also exists) is the classic way to give a project a text readout without needing a full graphics display. Wired directly, it needs a demanding 6+ control pins and a contrast-adjustment potentiometer; almost everyone instead uses a small I2C 'backpack' board soldered to the back, which reduces the whole interface to just two wires (SDA/SCL) plus power, at the cost of needing to know the backpack's I2C address and a library that speaks to it.
simpleSummary: A small screen that displays two lines of text, a simple way to show readouts without a full display.

specifications.interface: I2C via backpack (raw display uses a parallel interface without one)
specifications.characterGrid: 16 columns x 2 rows (20x4 variant also common)
specifications.contrastAdjustment: Trimpot on the I2C backpack board

pinMap.name: SCL
pinMap.gotcha: Common I2C backpack addresses are 0x27 or 0x3F — if the display shows nothing but backlight is on, an I2C scanner sketch is the fastest way to find the actual address.

useCases.title: Sensor readout display
useCases.scenario: Show live temperature, humidity, or other sensor readings without needing a computer connected.

useCases.title: Menu-driven device interface
useCases.scenario: Combine with a rotary encoder or buttons to build a simple menu system for a standalone device.

useCases.title: Status/debug display
useCases.scenario: Show system status or debug values during development without needing Serial Monitor.

oftenConfusedWith: OLED display (higher resolution graphics, not just fixed-grid characters)
oftenUpgradedTo: OLED display (SSD1306) for graphics, custom fonts, and better contrast
